subject: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@helixthera.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: devops@helixthera.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory

Hi Grace / Jordan,

Thanks again for making time for Helix's private deployment. We have our cutover window target of 2027-04-14 and would like to run an end-to-end dry-run next week to validate connectivity, routing, and the smoke traffic profile. The dry-run scope we want covered:
- VPC peering / cross-account routing sanity
- VPN / IPSec tunnel bring-up from our transit (we'll provide PSKs)
- NAT/Egress and allowlist verification for Redwood service IPs
- Bastion + engineer access and SSH key handoff
- Small sample inference traffic (1000 tokens/min) to validate batching and KV cache behavior

Can your team run a ~2 hour dry-run on 2027-04-12 or 2027-04-13 (PDT)? If not, propose alternatives. Attached is our initial access inventory template for your team to fill (IPs, contacts, certificate thumbprints).

Attachments: access-inventory-template.csv

Open items we want clarified during the dry-run: expected egress IP, port list for token traffic, and whether there are any intermediate proxies Redwood will require.

Appreciate it,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Therapeutics
---
Helix Therapeutics | sara.nguyen@helixthera.com
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@helixthera.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory

Sara — thanks for the clear scope. We can absolutely run a dry-run. 2027-04-13 09:00-11:00 PDT works best for our infra and networking leads. Proposed agenda (brief):
1) 09:00 — Introductions + success criteria confirmation
2) 09:15 — VPN bring-up and route advertisement validation
3) 09:45 — Firewall / NAT allowlist test (simple curl checks + egress verification)
4) 10:15 — Smoke inference traffic (1k tokens/min steady, 5-minute burst tests)
5) 10:40 — Failover + model-fallback sanity (if we throttle or induce errors)
6) 10:55 — Action items & next steps

Please populate the attached inventory sheet with your expected public IP ranges and SRE contacts. Jordan will collate and circulate a dry-run checklist (dryrun-checklist-v1.pdf) that we'll use during the session.

Quick asks for Helix prior to the run:
- Confirm the tunnel PSK and local/remote subnets for IPSec (we'll keep these in the secure Doc we share)
- Provide a test service account with minimal scopes for traffic generation (or let us create one scoped to the inference endpoint)

I'll loop in Networking for port-level details.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory — network specifics

Looping in the network/infra details so Helix has everything ahead of the dry-run. Key items:
- IPs to allow on Helix side: 34.201.12.45/32, 34.201.12.46/32 (Redwood egress pool for this tenant)
- Ports: 443 (TLS), 10250 (internal telemetry), 22 (bastion) — we also need outbound 443 to S3 endpoints for artifact pulls
- If you're peering via IPSec we'll establish BGP; advertise the /24 you intend to use. We will accept the routes but require a prefix filter to prevent long prefixes.
- Egress NAT behavior: we will NAT to the two egress IPs above; please confirm those are allowed in your firewall.
- MTU: set at 1420 for the tunnel to avoid fragmentation with VXLAN encapsulation on the transit side.
- For the smoke traffic, we'll simulate 1k tokens/min using a single test account; this will show batching efficiency. If you have a per-IP rate limit, let us know and we'll scope the test.

Attached: network-port-matrix.xlsx (port/protocol matrix + sample ACLs).

We will not place any of our control-plane endpoints on your private subnets — only the inference runtime egresses. If there are any regulatory egress controls Helix must enforce, flag them and we can route through a staging proxy.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Network Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@helixthera.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: devops@helixthera.com, ops+infra@helixthera.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory

Grace / Kimberly — thanks, that helps a lot. We're confirming the following for the 04-13 dry-run:
- Dry-run window: 2027-04-13 09:00-11:00 PDT
- Helix advertised prefix for BGP: 198.51.100.0/24 (will be announced from our transit)
- Tunnel PSK and pre-provisioned certs will be uploaded to the secure folder by 2027-04-08
- We've added the two Redwood egress IPs to our firewall staging policy and confirmed with our security team (screenshot pending)

I've attached our current tunnel config and the updated access inventory (filled where available). We couldn't confirm one CIDR for a legacy load balancer — marked in the sheet as TBD.

Attachments: tunnel-config-20270407.conf, access-inventory-completed.csv

Forwarded message included below for the run book and contacts.

Subject: Re: Edge acceptance dry-run & access inventory — day-of runbook and on-call

All — quick day-of checklist from Ops and the on-call roster so everyone's aligned:
- Day-of Slack channel: #privdeploy-helix-dryrun (we'll invite Helix SREs)
- Primary Redwood on-call: Ben Carter (pager: +1-415-555-0142)
- Secondary: Karthik Iyer (pager: +1-650-555-0199)
- Expected artifacts to hand back: dryrun-checklist-v1.pdf (filled), connectivity log (tar.gz), and a short postmortem if any failures occur
- Success criteria (quick): tunnel established, BGP route visible at both edges, test inference traffic completes with <200ms median latency and no token loss at 95th percentile

Links: runbook: DOCS-PRIVDEPLOY-4721/runbook-dryrun (will be shared as a Google Doc in the Slack channel)

If Helix confirms the uploaded tunnel config and the filled inventory, we'll mark the dry-run as booked and circulate calendar invites.

Thanks — see you on 4/13.
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Ops
Redwood Inference
